recent_hooks.hook: You typed "AI Advantage Bootcamp Reddit" into the search bar because you wanted one thing the webinar would never give you: a stranger with nothing to sell.
Did you ever notice that the AI Advantage webinar feels weirdly familiar even if you've never seen it before?
YouTube has a 47-minute video that teaches the exact ChatGPT workflow Igor Pogany walks you through in the AI Advantage Bootcamp. It is free. It has been free since before the webinar existed.
Picture the two browser tabs open on your laptop right now.
Fifteen hours. That is the number the AI Advantage webinar dangles in front of you like a carrot on a stick. Fifteen hours a week, back in your pocket, for the low investment of $995.
You paste your prompt, hit enter, and out comes something that sounds like a LinkedIn motivational poster wrote it after three coffees. Bland. Glossy. Nothing like how you actually talk.
You watched the webinar. You felt the pull. And then a quiet, stubborn voice in the back of your head asked the question nobody on that stage wanted you to ask: "Is there a free version of this?"

The price tag says $995. That number is the smallest part of what this actually costs you.
What happens if you take the bootcamp and only save 9 hours a week?
A course can be completely real and still leave a hole in the middle of you.
It is 8:58pm. You clicked the link two days ago for a "free AI summit," and now you are watching a countdown timer shrink while a friendly voice tells you the doors close at midnight.
You typed the program name into YouTube and got fourteen glowing reviews in a row, all wearing the same excited face, all using the same words, all linking to the same checkout page.
Remember when the answer to your money problems was supposed to be selling your own online course?
Dean Graziosi has sold something to almost everyone who has ever typed "how to make money online" into a search bar at 1am.
This is not the first time these two have stood on a stage together and pointed at a checkout button. Not even close.

Before you trust the guy promising to teach you AI, you should probably know he has never been famous for being good at AI.

Here is the question almost nobody asks out loud when a program gets a "2026 updated" label slapped on the sales page: did they rebuild the engine, or did they just repaint the car?
You sat through the webinar, the timer ticked toward zero, and somewhere around minute fifty a thought crossed your mind that you tried to push away: "I could probably just figure this out myself."
Can someone who still asks their kid to fix the TV remote actually learn AI in a six week program?
A guy worth tens of millions of dollars does not sit at his laptop typing prompts into ChatGPT at 11pm.
